sources.title: OPG reports 2025 first quarter financial results
sources.capture_method: Exact page text returned by web.open; direct scripted HTML request returned403.

claims.claim: In May 2025 OPG estimated the four-unit DNNP at $20.9B including interest,cost escalation and contingency; this is a project estimate rather than an overnight-capital estimate.
claims.evidence_quote: The total cost of the four-unit DNNP, including interest, cost escalation, and contingency, is currently estimated at approximately $20.9 billion.

claims.claim: The May 2025 first-unit release-quality budget was $7.7B including $6.1B for the reactor and $1.6B for shared systems/services.
claims.evidence_quote: The first unit SMR is expected to cost $6.1 billion, along with systems and services that would be common to all four SMRs planned as part of the project of $1.6 billion.

claims.claim: The $7.7B amount includes first-unit and shared infrastructure, not four units and not the reactor alone.
claims.evidence_quote: The total budget of $7.7 billion represents the release-quality estimate for both the first SMR and shared infrastructure.

sources.title: Darlington SMR: Project Update - Nov.10, 2026
sources.capture_method: Exact page text returned by web.open; dated project-update section in a maintained page; direct scripted HTML request returned403.

claims.claim: The Nov10, 2026 update withdraws the prior October 2030 commercial-operation target and prior budget for Unit1; keep the May 2025 $7.7B as historical.
claims.evidence_quote: Unit 1 is no longer expected to meet the previously disclosed October 2030 commercial-operation target or be completed within the previously disclosed budget.

claims.claim: OPG expects the cost/schedule assessment to be substantially complete by mid2027; the source does not provide a replacement budget.
claims.evidence_quote: This updated budget and schedule will be informed by a comprehensive assessment that is now underway and expected to be substantially complete by mid-2027.

sources.title: Electrically-Heated Demonstration Unit campaign complete
sources.capture_method: Direct public company-post HTML; datePublished2025-11-19T18:38:21.292Z in JSON-LD; transcript read as company-reported evidence.

claims.claim: Antares reports testing its electrically heated prototype with NASA Marshall in Huntsville. It is thermal hardware testing, not a nuclear criticality or electricity-producing reactor demonstration.
claims.evidence_quote: So we partnered with NASA Marshall and Huntsville, AL to test our electrically heated prototype.

claims.claim: The company describes the EDU as an electrically heated stand-in for its reactor core.
claims.evidence_quote: This unit is a full-scale, electrically heated stand-in for our core, built to push each heat pipe, interface, and material to real operating temperatures and pressures.
